key_insight: Preparing charge- and spin-adapted matrix product states directly from reduced tensors avoids dense tensor loading and substantially lowers quantum state-preparation costs.
engineering_relevance: Symmetry-aware loading can reduce fault-tolerant quantum resource requirements for correlated-electron simulations, although state preparation may still dominate downstream computation.
method: Load symmetry-allowed reduced blocks of a U(1) × SU(2)-symmetric MPS using Householder–LKS synthesis.
Apply Clebsch–Gordan coefficients to reconstruct magnetic degrees of freedom.
Avoid explicitly loading unfolded dense tensors.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks cover 4 × 4 and 4 × 6 Fermi–Hubbard states and molecular active spaces; at 15-bit rotation precision and the QROM-optimal point, molecular cases show approximately 14–54× fewer Toffolis, 20–87× lower active volume, and 33–140× lower Toffoli × qubit volume than dense MPS loading.
watch_item: Larger-lattice extrapolations suggest DMRG-state loading may exceed phase-estimation costs, motivating joint optimization of state fidelity, compression, and the initial-state ansatz.
paper_title: Quantum Loading of Charge and Spin-Adapted MPS
